# BR-002 — Sequence numbers

## Goal
Let users number files while renaming, e.g. `IMG_4411.jpg` → `Trip_001.jpg`.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1: `Rename-ByPattern` gets a `-Sequence` switch. When set, the token `{n}` in `-Replacement` is replaced by a running number starting at `-Start` (default 1), zero-padded to `-Pad` digits (default 3).
- AC-2: Files are numbered in ascending order of their current name (ordinal, case-insensitive), so the result is deterministic.
- AC-3: Without `-Sequence`, `{n}` is left as literal text (backward compatible with BR-001 behaviour and tests).
- AC-4: Tests in `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1` cover AC-1 to AC-3; all BR-001 tests still pass.

## Scope
- `src/BatchRename.psm1`
- new file `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1`

## Out of scope
- Changing `scripts/*.ps1`.

## Verification
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build.ps1`
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/test.ps1`

1	# PLAN
2	
3	## Understanding
4	Add sequence numbering to `Rename-ByPattern` in `src/BatchRename.psm1`. A new `-Sequence` switch makes the function replace the token `{n}` in `-Replacement` with a running number for each file. The number starts at `-Start` (default 1) and is zero-padded to `-Pad` digits (default 3). For example, `IMG_4411.jpg` becomes `Trip_001.jpg`. Matched files are numbered in ascending order of their current name, using an ordinal, case-insensitive comparison, so the result is deterministic. Without `-Sequence`, `{n}` stays as literal text and BR-001 behaviour and tests are unchanged. A new test file, `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1`, covers AC-1 to AC-3 using only the dependency-free helpers `Assert-Equal`, `Assert-True` and `New-TestFolder`. `scripts/*.ps1` is not changed.
5	
6	## Files likely involved
7	- src/BatchRename.psm1
8	- tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1
9	
10	## Steps
11	1. In `Rename-ByPattern`'s `param()` block, add `[switch]$Sequence`, `[ValidateRange(0, [int]::MaxValue)][int]$Start = 1` and `[ValidateRange(1, 9)][int]$Pad = 3`. Keep the existing parameters unchanged.
12	2. Right after the `$files = @(Get-ChildItem ... | Where-Object ...)` line, sort `$files` by name with an ordinal, case-insensitive comparison: `$keys = [string[]]@($files | ForEach-Object Name); [System.Array]::Sort($keys, $files, [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)`. Do not use `Sort-Object`, because it compares by culture. Sort in every mode; it only fixes the order, so BR-001 results are unchanged.
13	3. Before the `$plan = @(foreach ...)` loop, set `$n = $Start`. Inside the loop, before `[regex]::Replace`, build the per-file replacement: `$rep = $Replacement; if ($Sequence) { $rep = $Replacement.Replace('{n}', $n.ToString().PadLeft($Pad, '0')); $n++ }`. Then call `[regex]::Replace($file.Name, $Pattern, $rep)`. Increment the counter before the existing `continue` for unchanged names, so every matched file uses up exactly one number. Numbers longer than `-Pad` digits are not truncated.
14	4. Update the comment-based help `.SYNOPSIS`/add `.PARAMETER` notes briefly describing `-Sequence`, `-Start`, `-Pad` and the `{n}` token (match existing terse style).
15	5. Create `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1` in the same style as `RenameByPattern.Tests.ps1`, using fresh `New-TestFolder` folders:
16	  (a) AC-1/AC-2 defaults: files `IMG_4411.jpg`, `img_3000.jpg`, `IMG_0002.jpg`, plus `notes.md`, which does not match. Run with `-Pattern '(?i)^img_\d+' -Replacement 'Trip_{n}' -Sequence`. Expect IMG_0002→Trip_001.jpg, img_3000→Trip_002.jpg, IMG_4411→Trip_003.jpg; the files exist on disk and `notes.md` is unchanged.
17	  (b) AC-2 ordinal, case-insensitive order: files `b.txt`, `A.txt`, `file10.txt`, `file9.txt`. Run with `-Pattern '^.*(?=\.txt$)' -Replacement 'x{n}' -Sequence -Pad 1`. Expect A→x1, b→x2, file10→x3, file9→x4. A case-sensitive sort would put `A` differently, and a natural sort would put `file9` before `file10`.
18	  (c) AC-1 `-Start 7 -Pad 2`: two files become `_07` and `_08`. Also `-Start 100 -Pad 2` gives `100`, with no truncation.
19	  (d) AC-1 with `-WhatIf`: the returned objects show the numbered names, and the files on disk are unchanged.
20	  (e) AC-3: no `-Sequence`, file `a.txt`, `-Pattern '^a' -Replacement 'b{n}'`. Expect the new name `b{n}.txt` on disk. Passing `-Start`/`-Pad` without `-Sequence` also leaves `{n}` as literal text.
21	  In every case, find results by OldName or sort by OldName before asserting.
22	6. Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build.ps1` and `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/test.ps1`. Both must exit 0, and the BR-001 tests must still report `ok`.
23	
24	## Validation
25	- AC-1: Sequence.Tests.ps1 cases (a), (c) and (d) check that `{n}` is replaced by the zero-padded running number, using the default Start=1/Pad=3 and the custom values Start=7/Pad=2 and Start=100/Pad=2, both on disk and under `-WhatIf`.
26	- AC-2: Case (b) checks ordinal, case-insensitive numbering order (A before b; file10 before file9). Case (a) checks mixed-case IMG/img ordering.
27	- AC-3: Case (e) checks that `{n}` stays literal without `-Sequence`. The existing tests/RenameByPattern.Tests.ps1 and SafeFileName.Tests.ps1 pass unmodified.
28	- AC-4: `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/test.ps1` exits 0 with 'all tests passed'. `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build.ps1` exits 0 and reports that both functions are exported.
29	
30	## Risks
31	- `[System.Array]::Sort($keys, $items, $comparer)` overload resolution in PowerShell: it should bind to the non-generic `Sort(Array, Array, IComparer)`. If binding fails, fall back to `$files = @($files | Sort-Object { $_.Name.ToUpperInvariant() } -CaseSensitive -Culture '')`, or to a `List[object]` with an explicit comparison. Note that invariant culture is still not strictly ordinal, so Array.Sort is preferred.
32	- When `$files` is empty, the key/item arrays have length 0. Array.Sort handles this, but it must not throw under StrictMode Latest; wrapping in `@()` guards this.
33	- Numbered targets can collide with existing files, e.g. renaming into a folder that already has Trip_001.jpg, or reshuffling already-numbered files. The existing collision check throws before anything is renamed. This is safe but can surprise users, and a rename-in-place swap is not supported.
34	- A file whose computed name equals its current name still uses up a number (it is skipped after numbering). This keeps numbering tied to position in the sorted list.
35	
36	## Assumptions
37	- Numbering covers every file that matches `-Pattern`, in sorted order, including files whose final name ends up unchanged.
38	- If `{n}` appears more than once in `-Replacement`, or the pattern matches more than once in one name, every occurrence in that file gets the same number.
39	- `-Start` must be >= 0 and `-Pad` must be in the range 1–9. Numbers wider than `-Pad` are left as they are, not truncated.
40	- `-Start`/`-Pad` are ignored without `-Sequence`.
41	- Sorting the matched files always, not only with `-Sequence`, is acceptable. It only makes the output order deterministic, and the BR-001 tests already sort the results.
42	
43	## Open questions
44	- Should `-Start`/`-Pad` without `-Sequence` raise an error instead of being silently ignored? The plan ignores them.
45

- tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1

Do not use `Sort-Object`, because it compares by culture. Sort in every mode; it only fixes the order, so BR-001 results are unchanged.
3. Before the `$plan = @(foreach ...)` loop, set `$n = $Start`. Then call `[regex]::Replace($file.Name, $Pattern, $rep)`. Increment the counter before the existing `continue` for unchanged names, so every matched file uses up exactly one number. Numbers longer than `-Pad` digits are not truncated.
4. Update the comment-based help `.SYNOPSIS`/add `.PARAMETER` notes briefly describing `-Sequence`, `-Start`, `-Pad` and the `{n}` token (match existing terse style).
5. Create `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1` in the same style as `RenameByPattern.Tests.ps1`, using fresh `New-TestFolder` folders:
  (a) AC-1/AC-2 defaults: files `IMG_4411.jpg`, `img_3000.jpg`, `IMG_0002.jpg`, plus `notes.md`, which does not match. Run with `-Pattern '(?i)^img_\d+' -Replacement 'Trip_{n}' -Sequence`. Expect IMG_0002→Trip_001.jpg, img_3000→Trip_002.jpg, IMG_4411→Trip_003.jpg; the files exist on disk and `notes.md` is unchanged.

  (d) AC-1 with `-WhatIf`: the returned objects show the numbered names, and the files on disk are unchanged.

## Validation
- AC-1: Sequence.Tests.ps1 cases (a), (c) and (d) check that `{n}` is replaced by the zero-padded running number, using the default Start=1/Pad=3 and the custom values Start=7/Pad=2 and Start=100/Pad=2, both on disk and under `-WhatIf`.

+++ b/src/BatchRename.psm1
@@ -19,18 +19,35 @@ function Rename-ByPattern {
     <#
     .SYNOPSIS
       Rename matching files in one folder after checking all target names for collisions.
+    .PARAMETER Sequence
+      Replace {n} tokens with numbers in ordinal, case-insensitive file name order.
+    .PARAMETER Start
+      First sequence number (default 1). Ignored without -Sequence.
+    .PARAMETER Pad
+      Minimum sequence number width (default 3). Ignored without -Sequence.
     #>
     [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
     param(
         [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path,
         [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Pattern,
-        [Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowEmptyString()][string]$Replacement
+        [Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowEmptyString()][string]$Replacement,
+        [switch]$Sequence,
+        [ValidateRange(0, [int]::MaxValue)][int]$Start = 1,
+        [ValidateRange(1, 9)][int]$Pad = 3
     )
 
     $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -File -ErrorAction Stop |
         Where-Object { [regex]::IsMatch($_.Name, $Pattern) })
+    $keys = [string[]]@($files | ForEach-Object { $_.Name })
+    [System.Array]::Sort($keys, $files, [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
+    $n = $Start
     $plan = @(foreach ($file in $files) {
-        $new = ConvertTo-SafeFileName ([regex]::Replace($file.Name, $Pattern, $Replacement))
+        $rep = $Replacement
+        if ($Sequence) {
+            $rep = $Replacement.Replace('{n}', $n.ToString().PadLeft($Pad, '0'))
+            $n++
+        }
+        $new = ConvertTo-SafeFileName ([regex]::Replace($file.Name, $Pattern, $rep))
         if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($new)) {
             throw "Empty target name for '$($file.Name)'"
         }

input.summary: The implementation follows the plan: new parameters, an Array.Sort with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, numbering per file, and {n} left literal without -Sequence. Build and tests pass (VERIFY_RESULT pass=true). The problem is the AC-2 ordering test. It expects '_first.txt' to sort first (x1), and the run reports that as ok. But .NET OrdinalIgnoreCase folds to UPPERCASE, and '_' (0x5F) is greater than 'Z' (0x5A), so a true ordinal case-insensitive sort puts '_first.txt' last. So either the sort does not bind or behave as intended at runtime, or the test expectation is wrong and passes anyway. In both cases, AC-2 behaviour is not actually shown. Also, the test comment says the names separate ordinal from culture sorting, but every name in that test sorts the same way under culture comparison, so the test cannot catch a culture-based sort. Please fix this and add a case that tells the two apart.

Lines 45-49 replace '{n}' with $n.ToString().PadLeft($Pad,'0') and increment. In tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1, the defaults loop (Trip_001..003, with and without -WhatIf) and the start-7/100 loop (_07/_08, _100/_101 with no truncation) all report ok in VERIFY_RESULT.json.

src/BatchRename.psm1:41-42 calls [System.Array]::Sort($keys, $files, [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase). But tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1:75 expects '_first.txt' -> 'x1.txt', and VERIFY_RESULT reports 'ok   sequence: ordinal _first.txt'. OrdinalIgnoreCase compares uppercase-folded chars, and '_' (0x5F) > 'Z' (0x5A), so an ordinal case-insensitive order would be A, b, file10, file9, Z, _first. The observed order matches culture sorting instead. Also, none of the chosen names sort differently under culture and ordinal-ignore-case comparison apart from this one, so ordinal ordering is not reliably shown.

src/BatchRename.psm1:45 sets $rep = $Replacement, which is only changed inside if ($Sequence). tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1:98-105 checks that 'b{n}.txt' is produced both with no options and with Start=7/Pad=2 but no -Sequence. The 'literal name/target exists' checks and all BR-001 tests pass (test.ps1 exit 0, 'all tests passed').

tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1 exists and covers AC-1 and AC-3. scripts/test.ps1 exits 0 with 'all tests passed', and build.ps1 exits 0 ('build ok: exported ConvertTo-SafeFileName, Rename-ByPattern'). However, the AC-2 coverage (lines 69-81) cannot tell ordinal from culture ordering, and its '_first.txt' expectation contradicts OrdinalIgnoreCase semantics, so AC-2 is not properly covered.

issues.description: The expected order puts '_first.txt' first (x1). StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase folds to uppercase, and '_' (U+005F) sorts after 'Z' (U+005A), so ordinal case-insensitive order is A, b, file10, file9, Z, _first (_first -> x6). The test passes with _first -> x1, which means one of two things. Either the runtime order is not OrdinalIgnoreCase (for example, the Array.Sort overload binding does not sort $files in place, or some other ordering is in effect), which would be an AC-2 defect in src/BatchRename.psm1:41-42. Or the expectation is wrong and somehow still passes. Please check the actual order, for example by printing $files names after the Sort, then fix the implementation or the expectation to match true ordinal, case-insensitive order.

The comment says this case includes names that distinguish ordinal from culture sorting, but A/b/file10/file9/Z/_first all sort the same way under culture (InvariantCulture/current culture) comparison as the test expects. So a Sort-Object/culture-based implementation would also pass. Add names whose order differs between the two, for example 'a-c.txt' vs 'ab.txt' (ordinal: '-' 0x2D < 'B', so a-c comes first; culture gives hyphens little weight, so ab comes first), or '_x' vs letters with the correct uppercase-fold expectation.

issues.description: The expected order puts '_first.txt' first (x1). StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase folds to uppercase, and '_' (U+005F) sorts after 'Z' (U+005A), so ordinal case-insensitive order is A, b, file10, file9, Z, _first (_first -> x6). The test passes with _first -> x1, which means one of two things. Either the runtime order is not OrdinalIgnoreCase (for example, the Array.Sort overload binding does not sort $files in place, or some other ordering is in effect), which would be an AC-2 defect in src/BatchRename.psm1:41-42. Or the expectation is wrong and somehow still passes. Please check the actual order, for example by printing $files names after the Sort, then fix the implementation or the expectation to match true ordinal, case-insensitive order.

The comment says this case includes names that distinguish ordinal from culture sorting, but A/b/file10/file9/Z/_first all sort the same way under culture (InvariantCulture/current culture) comparison as the test expects. So a Sort-Object/culture-based implementation would also pass. Add names whose order differs between the two, for example 'a-c.txt' vs 'ab.txt' (ordinal: '-' 0x2D < 'B', so a-c comes first; culture gives hyphens little weight, so ab comes first), or '_x' vs letters with the correct uppercase-fold expectation.
